items_missed: No agenda statement — 'do you have a moment to go over that?' is a permission ask, not a roadmap; no gather-details-then-pricing sequence, no 10-15 minute timeframe, no 'sound good?'

Save Your Ass prep speech entirely absent — no 'prep before move day means a shorter move and a lower bill', no consolidation examples (loose drawer items, kids' toys, photos off walls), no take-a-carload tip, no closing sense-check. Full 10 points lost.

Estimate reasoning was contradictory and landed high. The customer volunteered that Einstein moved her in about two hours; Bri said 'the system quoted you about four hours. So if it took about two I would almost estimate between 4:00 and five', then reversed to 'three and a half to four and a half hours' with no explanation of what changed

Two elevator-access one-bedrooms ten minutes apart, with a reserved elevator and a ten-foot walk to the door, was never reconciled against the customer's own two-hour data point — the strongest accuracy signal on the call went unused
Asked about the two TVs but never said how they would be handled or what they add to the time — no padding/wrapping offer at all
Never asked about additional stops or storage stops
Never asked about additional rooms (storage unit, balcony, garage)
No 'no hidden fees' pitch — no credit card fees, no transportation fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees all went unsaid
No sense-check after the clock explanation — went straight from prorated increments into the estimate
Did not explain the bolded detail list at the top of the confirmation email, and never asked the customer to reply with corrections
Did not give hours of operation or how to reach the team
Used the customer's name only twice, both in the opening
Insurance explanation stopped at No Worries $2,000 — no 60 cents/lb baseline for contrast
Differentiator block was delivered before any move details were confirmed, which made it read as a script recital rather than a response to this customer's move
Misspoke the feature name as 'major mover feature' instead of Meet Your Mover, and fumbled the drive time live ('about half hour drive, nope, ten minutes')
top_strength: Bri worked the access details harder than most reps do, and that is the part of this call worth keeping. She captured both unit numbers, both floors, the 50-foot truck-to-elevator walk at each end, the 10-foot elevator-to-door walk, and then asked the question almost nobody asks: 'And are these freight elevators? Are they just the general use elevators?' — surfacing that Shannon can reserve the elevator for exclusive use. She also used the repeat-customer angle well, asking 'Do you remember how long it took us to get you into that apartment,' which handed her a real two-hour benchmark. All three differentiators, the hourly rate, the inclusions list, and the full clock explanation including the 2.5-hour minimum were all delivered.
coaching_note: The single highest-leverage fix is the Save Your Ass speech, which is missing entirely and is worth ten points on its own: 'Shannon, the biggest thing that controls your final bill is how prepared you are when we walk in. We're fast with big furniture and boxes; we slow down on loose items — drawers, lamps, things off the walls. Anything small enough to fit in your car, take a carload over yourself and you'll knock real time off the clock. Does that make sense?' That is thirty seconds, and on a two-elevator move it is the difference between a four-hour bill and a three-hour one. Second: you had the answer to your own estimate question and talked past it. When Shannon said her last Einstein move took two hours max, that is the number to build from — say 'the system says four, but you've done this with us before at two hours, and we're going elevator to elevator ten minutes apart, so I'd put you at two and a half to three and a half.' Instead the quote moved up to four-to-five, then to three-and-a-half-to-four-and-a-half, with no reason given, and a customer who hears the number change twice stops trusting it. Third: run the confirmation-email close properly — the bolded details at the top, 'reply with any corrections', no deposit required, and our hours. Finally, move the differentiator block after the details are confirmed so it answers her move instead of arriving cold in the first ninety seconds.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and pleasant with one real rapport attempt (the husband-TV-size joke) and a nice 'super convenient' affirmation, but largely transactional and script-forward — the differentiator recital came before any listening, and several phrases came out garbled.
audio_review_reason: Transcript turn-ordering is badly interleaved (Shannon's 'This is she?' and 'Doing well. How are you?' land after Bri's next lines, and several yes-answers appear stacked), so pace, talk-over, and whether Bri was stepping on the customer cannot be judged from text alone.
